newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa minister defends import tariff cuts.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa minister defends import tariff cuts.

text.p: Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin on Thursday defended government's drive to cut import tariffs and said that it had helped to reduce inflation and create more competitive industries.

In a special debate in parliament, he said that tariff cuts in recent years had been a response to South Africa's needs and not merely a response to the requirements of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade.

The debate was based on a report prepared by the parliamentary trade and industry committee in response to widespread criticism that tariff cuts had created unemployment by destroying some industries, and were not being matched by enough measures to help firms become more competitive.
"We have already seen the very positive effects of the liberalisation of the economy," Erwin said.

"It helped bring down inflation to consistently single digit levels, improved the cost of living for the very poor and the unemployed, and even led to the local production of some of the cheapest quality motor cars in the world."
Industries such as textiles and vehicle manufacturing, which have been hard hit by tariff cuts, were now making some of the biggest new investments in the South African economy, he said.
